A system is ultrastable, in W. Ross Ashby's sense, when two loops keep its essential variables inside bounds: a fast loop that corrects disturbance, and a slow loop that changes the system itself when the fast loop cannot.

The slow loop reads the same variables every tick, and when one has been out of bounds for two ticks in a row it takes one discrete step on that variable's ladder, keeps the step only if the variable comes back, and otherwise undoes it and takes the next.
